title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 6th District
area: Central Kentucky, including Lexington, Frankfort and Richmond.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Andy Barr (R) ran for U.S. Senate instead of re-election to this seat and did not appear on the District 6 primary ballot.

Ralph Alvarado defeated Ryan Dotson, Greg Plucinski, Steve Shannon and Adam Perez Arquette in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Zach Dembo defeated Cherlynn Stevenson, Erin Petrey and four other candidates in the Democratic primary.

priorities.text: "My entire career has been devoted to public service, whether as a Navy JAG officer, a federal prosecutor protecting constitutional rights and fighting crime, or as a teacher in an underserved community. But after seeing the corruption in Washington D.C. and this Administration's abuse of the criminal justice system, I knew that my public service needed to take a different path."

positions.summary: Priorities page calls for reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring and expanding ACA tax credits, and a public option.
positions.quote: In Congress, I’ll fight to restore and expand ACA tax credits so that health insurance remains within reach for working families.

positions.summary: Priorities page says he would be a vote to codify Roe v. Wade and protect IVF.
positions.quote: I would be a vote to codify Roe v. Wade, which worked for over 50 years, and protect fertility treatments like IVF.

positions.summary: Priorities page calls tariffs taxes on businesses and consumers and says he would fight to end the trade war.
positions.quote: In Congress, I’ll fight to end this senseless trade war, support free and open trade that helps our farmers and distillers compete globally,

positions.summary: Priorities page says everyone should make a living wage of at least $15 an hour and notes Congress has not raised the minimum wage in 17 years.
positions.quote: Everyone should make a living wage of at least $15 an hour

positions.summary: Priorities page calls ICE overfunded and undersupervised, wants it focused on violent criminals rather than law-abiding people, and supports a path to citizenship.
positions.quote: The firing of Kristi Noem was long overdue and in no way addresses the underlying problems with that overfunded and undersupervised agency.

priorities.text: "Healthcare isn't a talking point to me — it's been my life's work. In Congress, I'll work with both parties to fight for affordable healthcare, lower costs, and practical solutions that help Kentucky families."

positions.summary: Voted yes on SB 9, which banned abortion once a fetal heartbeat is detectable, with exceptions.
Voted yes on SB 150, which eliminated Kentucky's permit requirement to carry a concealed deadly weapon.
Voted yes on HB 563, which created a tax-credit scholarship program funding private-school tuition and other education expenses for Kentucky students.

record.text: Chaired the Kentucky Senate Health and Welfare Committee during the 2019-2020 and 2021-2022 legislative sessions.
Voted yes on SB 9 (banning abortion once a fetal heartbeat is detectable, with limited exceptions), which passed the Kentucky Senate 31-6 on February 14, 2019.
Voted yes on SB 150 (eliminating the permit requirement to carry a concealed deadly weapon in Kentucky), which passed the Kentucky Senate 29-8 on February 14, 2019.
Voted yes on HB 563 (creating a tax-credit scholarship program funding private-school tuition and other education expenses), which passed the Kentucky Senate 21-15 on March 16, 2021.

priorities.text: "As someone who's studied and taught political science for nearly a decade, he understands that the fundamental problem in American politics is campaign funding."

Also supports a moratorium on AI data centers, restricting police access to license-plate-reader data such as Flock cameras without a warrant, moving toward Medicare for All, building affordable housing, cutting funding for Israel, and criminal justice reform to end mass incarceration.
Lists campaign finance reform, lobbying and political corruption first among his "Top Policy Priorities", followed by data centers and AI, Medicare for All and affordable housing.

positions.summary: Policies page calls for Medicare for All, including universal coverage.
positions.quote: Provide universal healthcare coverage for all Americans

positions.summary: Policies page calls for taxing billionaires and raising the corporate tax rate.
positions.quote: Raise the corporate tax rate to 50% and use the new tax revenue to fund an United States Profit Dividend, which will be distributed equally among all adult Americans.

positions.summary: Policies page calls for capping rent increases on corporate-owned rental properties.
positions.quote: Cap rent increases for corporate-owned rental properties

positions.summary: Policies page calls for amending the War Powers Resolution so only Congress decides on war.
positions.quote: Amend the War Powers Resolution to so that only Congress can decide whether to go to war or begin new military engagements

positions.summary: Policies page calls for ending funding for Israel's military.
positions.quote: Stop funding Israel's military and require all lobbyists that advocate for the interests of foreing countries to register as agents under the FARA

statements.quote: Abolish ICE and replace it with in immigration enforcement organization that respects human life and the rule of law
statements.context: On his campaign website policies page

statements.quote: Invest in solar, wind, and other renewables in rural and underserved areas
statements.context: On his campaign website policies page, under clean energy

statements.quote: Implement minimum wages that reflect local living wages, with annual adjustments based on local cost of living changes
statements.context: On his campaign website policies page

priorities.text: Says he will work for young Kentuckians, focusing on fiscal responsibility and reducing what he calls wasteful spending.

positions.summary: Campaign agriculture page calls for reversing course on tariffs.
positions.quote: Reverse the course: On tariffs and other economically restrictive measures.

positions.summary: Issues page calls for a single-payer universal health care system.
positions.quote: Design a single-payer healthcare system that covers essential medical services, such as preventive care, hospitalization, prescription drugs, and long-term care

positions.summary: Issues page calls for raising the federal minimum wage and indexing it to inflation.
positions.quote: Raise the minimum wage: Increase the federal minimum wage to a level that reflects the cost of living in different regions, and index it to inflation to ensure it keeps pace with rising costs.

priorities.text: Campaign site headings include "Raise Minimum Wage To $15/Hr", "Health Care For All With Focus On Free Preventive Care" and "Reform Water, Electric & Utility Services For All".

positions.summary: Campaign site lists raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour.
Campaign site lists expanding Medicaid to cover more low-income residents.
positions.quote: Expand Medicaid to cover more low-income residents.

statements.quote: Invest in renewable energy projects to create jobs and protect natural resources.

researchNotes: Open seat: Andy Barr, the sitting representative, ran for U.S. Senate instead. No detailed issue positions beyond general priorities were found for Dembo or Bowman. No public information beyond his name on the ballot was found for write-in candidate Robert Quigley. Update (2026-10-19): added candidate-website statements for Pete Lynch (policies page), Jay Bowman (issues and agriculture pages; Ballotpedia survey cited earlier) and Robert Quigley (campaign website policy lists, which are headings rather than detailed plans). No Bowman page on abortion, guns or immigration was found. Biographical information for Lynch and Bowman comes from their own Ballotpedia survey responses; no independent coverage was found, and none beyond his name on the ballot for Quigley.
